before.popoverText: How: The shipped default: rulings are selected from a small set of discrete coverage rungs at one constant pen weight, so tone is carried by which rulings are drawn.Strengths: The measured baseline every other fill style is judged against.Weaknesses: One draw/skip verdict per ruling, so its coverage steps are visible and it cannot reach a deep shadow.

after.popoverText: How: The shipped ladder selects rulings from a small set of discrete coverage rungs; fineLadder keeps that mechanism and only increases the rung count (about 0.02 coverage per rung, derived from the ladder's own range), pushing the visible step below the visual threshold instead of removing it.Strengths: The minimal, lowest-risk change to the shipped default — same mechanism, one derived constant, zero free ends, only 61 paths.Weaknesses: Still a density law with one draw/skip verdict per ruling: R2 0.032, L* span 7.5, darkest L* 79.4 on sphere·hatch, and spacing CoV 0.678 with a 2x adjacent spacing step.

before.popoverText: How: The interlock: neighbouring rulings carry a chart-space lateral wave in ANTI-PHASE, each crest pointing into its neighbour's trough. Amplitude is capped live at the clearance the plot floor allows — the "minimum open space" figure the Round 5 study reports.Strengths: The round's anti-phase reference point: darkest L* 50.9 on sphere·hatch with 1253 mm of ink and 752 pen-downs, and a median darks clearance of 1.30 mm.Weaknesses: Its amplitude collapses to near zero in the lit region (0.3% of the shadow mean retained) because k = wvRamp(I) goes to zero above the light threshold — a straight ruling in the highlight, the defect the whole Round 6 wave family was built to fix — and unintended bare area is the worst of the wave laws measured (34.1%).
